title: Producing a totally ramified finite Galois extension that either solves the ramification weakly or puts the degree p extension on finite level
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a tower A inside B inside C of discrete valuation rings with A of mixed characteristic, A to B weakly unramified, B containing a primitive p-th root of unity and the top extension Galois of degree p, and concludes the existence of a finite Galois extension of K, totally ramified over A, that either is a weak solution for the tower or makes the top extension one of finite level (statement lines 35087-35100). The proof is a case analysis driven by Kummer theory and by the order of the element whose p-th root generates the top extension: in the case where that order is prime to p a totally ramified degree p extension is built so that the compositum has the required weak unramifiedness, and in the remaining case the base is replaced so as to reduce to a unit, after which either the residue class is not a p-th power and weak unramifiedness follows from the pre-purely-inseparable case, or the equation can be brought to the form y^p = 1 + pi b, which exhibits finite level with an explicit element (proof lines 35102-35139). Both alternatives of the conclusion are produced by explicit constructions. The counted span refers four times, three of them to earlier results of this chapter and one to Kummer theory in another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
